findings.statement: The legacy facade returns `getTokenSilently()` bare — no interceptor, no dedup, no explicit failure route; refresh is inherited from Auth0's silent-refresh mechanism.
Cognito-specific claim shapes (`cognito:groups`, `custom:tenantId`) are read only inside the adapter and mapped onto the domain `Principal`.
Auth0's namespaced custom-claim URL key is read inline in an application component — vendor-specific claim shape has crossed the boundary into the UI layer.
The Cognito adapter reads the access token (not the ID token) and attaches it to outbound requests as a Bearer credential.

No policy layer (`can(principal, action, resource)`, `hasRole`, etc.) wraps authorization decisions; `Principal.roles` is mapped by the adapter but nothing enforces role checks through a shared function. The new components don't check roles yet — so no inline reads exist today, but the pattern isn't set.
Hard-coded role strings are checked inline in an application component — no policy layer between vendor claims and the authorization decision.

`getTokenSilently()` is called with no `audience` anywhere — per the Auth0 profile, this yields an opaque (non-JWT) token that is not a valid API access token; the documented anti-pattern signalling the app is leaning on the ID token or a non-validating API for authorization.

cognito.note: Amplify v6: `setKeyValueStorage(sessionStorage)` where `sessionStorage` is the built-in from `aws-amplify/utils` — the profile's look-alike trap. Selects session over local storage; NOT a custom adapter. Tokens remain vendor-managed and JS-readable.

storage.recommended_seam: A domain storage interface fronted by the boundary. For Cognito: a user-defined class implementing `KeyValueStorageInterface` (from `aws-amplify/utils`) passed to `setKeyValueStorage`. For Auth0: a class implementing `ICache` passed via `cache:` on `createAuth0Client`. Application code depends on the domain interface only; storage is a swap of one wire in each adapter.

cost_evidence.basis: Cognito storage is one wire in a single adapter file (src/auth/adapters/cognito.ts:22) — swapping the selector for a user-defined class is a local edit inside the boundary. Auth0 storage is not configured at all, so becoming owned is one option on `createAuth0Client` in one facade file. The Cognito boundary keeps consumers from touching storage directly; the Auth0 side has no such shielding, so any Auth0 storage change also has to route through a new boundary before it becomes local.

cognito.note: Owned shape: 401-interceptor in `createApiClient` + `onSessionExpired` failure path, driven by `fetchAuthSession({ forceRefresh: true })`. Missing: single-flight dedup — N concurrent 401s would fire N refreshes.

auth0.note: Bare `getTokenSilently()` in the legacy facade; no interceptor, no dedup, no explicit failure route — refresh is inherited from Auth0's silent-refresh mechanism.

refresh.recommended_seam: For Cognito: keep the existing 401-retry pattern and add a single-flight refresh promise on the adapter (concurrent 401s await the same in-flight refresh). For Auth0: route the legacy facade's token acquisition through an `AuthPort` on the same client so the 401/single-flight/failure path is shared across vendors, or explicitly retire the legacy path as the migration completes.

cost_evidence.basis: Cognito is close to owned — the interceptor and failure path exist in src/api/client.ts and the port; single-flight is one field + a promise-caching guard on the adapter. Auth0's inherited path is called from one facade file (src/legacy/auth0-helpers.ts:31), but the retrofit isn't `getTokenSilently` itself — every caller of `getLegacyToken` needs to move onto the port to escape the inherited behavior; the cost scales with how many callers exist outside the audited surface.

cognito.note: Cognito-specific claim shapes (`cognito:groups`, `custom:tenantId`) read only inside the adapter and mapped to `Principal`.

auth0.note: Namespaced-claim URL key read inline in a component; Auth0's `User` type is the component's state type and the facade's return type — provider-specific coupling has spread beyond any adapter.

identity_provider.recommended_seam: All vendor-specific claim reads confined to per-vendor adapters (Cognito's `cognito:*`/`custom:*` keys and Auth0's namespaced URL keys), each projecting onto the domain `Principal`. App code speaks `Principal` only; no component ever names a Cognito or Auth0 claim key.

cost_evidence.basis: Cognito's provider-specific surface is fully localized to one file. Auth0's confirmed leak count is small in this fixture (one inline namespaced-claim read at src/components/LegacyAdmin.tsx:17, one `User`-typed component, one facade returning `User`/`Auth0Client`) — but the retrofit is per component-touch, not per adapter. Cost scales with how many Auth0-consuming files exist elsewhere; the pattern is the calcification, not the count.

cognito.note: The adapter reads the access token and maps roles into `Principal.roles`, but no policy layer wraps authorization decisions. The new components don't currently check roles, so nothing has inlined yet — but nothing prevents them from doing so; the boundary is present without an authorization API.

auth0.note: Hard-coded role strings checked inline in a component; the outbound token is opaque (`getTokenSilently()` with no `audience`) — the profile's documented anti-pattern indicating likely reliance on the ID token or a non-validating API.

authorization.recommended_seam: A single policy layer, e.g. `can(principal, action, resource)`, called from app code and backed by `Principal` alone. Both adapters project vendor claims onto `Principal`; no component reads vendor-specific claim shapes. For Auth0 specifically: pass `authorizationParams: { audience: <api-identifier> }` to `getAccessTokenSilently` (v2 shape) so the SDK returns a real JWT access token; then send that token, not the ID token.

cost_evidence.basis: Two independent problems compound. (1) The opaque-token anti-pattern (src/legacy/auth0-helpers.ts:31) is systemic — every API call authorized by `getLegacyToken` is authenticating with a non-JWT token; adding `audience` requires an API identifier decision, backend acceptance of the new audience, and re-consenting scopes. (2) There is no shared policy layer on either side; unification means projecting two vendors' claims onto `Principal` AND introducing an authorization function AND migrating each inline role check (src/components/LegacyAdmin.tsx:19) through it.

judgment_calls.context: Cognito is one wire from a custom adapter (built-in selector today, look-alike trap); Auth0 has no storage configured. Whether either matters depends on your storage goals.

judgment_calls.question: Is owning refresh (401-interceptor + single-flight + explicit failure path) on the roadmap, independent of any storage change?
judgment_calls.context: Cognito refresh is already partially owned — single-flight is the visible gap. Auth0 refresh is inherited via `getTokenSilently` and travels through the legacy facade.

judgment_calls.question: Is finishing the Auth0 → Cognito migration realistic in the next 12–24 months, or is Auth0 staying indefinitely?
judgment_calls.context: The 'right' scope of remediation on the Auth0 side depends on whether the legacy code is dying. If Auth0 is staying, its calcification needs the same boundary treatment as Cognito; if it's exiting soon, the migration completion IS the remediation.

judgment_calls.question: Are authorization model changes (RBAC/ABAC, finer permissions) planned — and, separately, is the ID→access-token fix for Auth0 already being tracked?
judgment_calls.context: The Auth0 opaque-token issue is independent of any broader authz change and moves at its own cadence (backend acceptance, audience assignment, scope consent). A policy layer would unify Cognito and Auth0 authorization but only pays off if either the model is changing or the migration is completing.

synthesis.posture: mid-migration — Cognito side bounded but incomplete; Auth0 side calcified

headline.text: The Cognito surface has a real boundary — `AuthPort`, an adapter with vendor types confined, access token attached, and a 401-retry path — but three gaps stop it short of fully bounded: storage uses the built-in `sessionStorage` selector (the look-alike trap, not a custom adapter), refresh has no single-flight dedup, and nothing tests the port contract. Meanwhile the Auth0 legacy path is calcified in every direction: `User`/`Auth0Client` types cross into a component's state, a namespaced-claim URL key is read inline, and API calls authorize with `getTokenSilently()` — no `audience` — which per the Auth0 profile yields an opaque token, the documented anti-pattern. Any single verdict would be wrong; the two surfaces are at different stages, and the highest-leverage moves live on the Auth0 side.
